title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 6

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Where will the public talk be held?
tasks.audioText: The town environment office is inviting students to a public talk about air quality. It will be held at the science centre on Thursday at four fifteen. A researcher will explain how traffic, heating and weather can affect pollution levels. Students who want to ask a question should send it to the organiser by Wednesday lunchtime.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. By when should students send questions?

A researcher will explain how traffic, heating and weather can affect pollution levels. Students who want to ask a question should send it to the organiser by Wednesday lunchtime.

tasks.prompt: A group of students measured air quality near three busy roads and one park. They recorded the results at the same time on several weekdays to make the comparison fair. The readings were usually higher beside the roads, but wind direction affected some results. The students explained that their small study could show a local pattern, not prove that traffic was the only cause of pollution. Reading 1. Why did students take readings at the same time?
options: To avoid measuring during rush hour
To collect readings only when the weather was clear
Their equipment could not measure traffic levels
Their study showed a local pattern but could not prove traffic was the only cause
They had measured only one road
Their study showed a local pattern but could not prove traffic was the only cause

tasks.prompt: The readings were higher near the road, ___ the wind was blowing towards the park.
Choose TWO factors that may influence local air quality.
options: The number of seats in a library

tasks.prompt: A measurement showing the level of pollution in the air is a pollution ___.
You are presenting the study results. Which statement is appropriately cautious?
options: Our small study proves that traffic is the only cause of pollution.
Our results suggest a local pattern, but further measurements are needed.
The data are perfect and cannot be questioned.
We did not collect enough information, so no discussion is possible.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of urban air quality in a logical order.
options: Choose locations and a consistent time
correctOrder: Choose locations and a consistent time

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how a college group could investigate local air quality. Describe what to measure and one limitation.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response describes a plausible local air-quality investigation and identifies relevant measurements (0–2); it explains one meaningful limitation, such as sampling location, timing or instrument uncertainty (0–2); the method is presented clearly with understandable grammar (0–2); air-quality/measurement vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
